title: Solo dev + AI: a persistent naval MMO in the browser, 1720s Caribbean (3D battles, economy, PvP)
author: bimbimejia93
selftext:
I've been building Tierra Firme, a persistent browser game where you captain a fleet in the 1720s Caribbean, pretty much entirely with AI as my dev team. The clip is a real fight from the live game: my flagship, the Princesa, leading a line of three against pirate raiders.

How AI fits in:

• Code: almost all of it written with Claude. The game is one big web client plus a Node server for multiplayer battles, saves and trades. I describe the design, it implements, I playtest and push back.

• Art: the port paintings, ship portraits, icons and talent medallions are AI-generated, then cleaned up and kept in one consistent painterly style.

• Balancing and analytics: I use AI to read player retention data, simulate battles to tune difficulty, and check the economy for exploits.

What's in the game:

• Real-time sea battles in 3D (or on a 2D chart): wind, points of sail, raking fire, boarding, ship powers and talent trees.

• A living economy: every port has its own market, plus contracts, warehouses, workshops, and ships built from the timber and canvas you bring.

• Multiplayer: squadrons that hunt pirate fleets, trading companies with forts on the coast, letters of marque, duels and arena PvP.

Free in the browser, desktop or phone: [playtierrafirme.com](http://playtierrafirme.com)

Happy to answer anything about the workflow: what works, what breaks, and where AI still needs a lot of hand-holding.
